clue.text: Cloth that's small for top of beer mug

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of the first letter of the word beer, so that opening letter is swapped out

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, a sucker
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A drinker's beer mug, perhaps made of some small piece of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: BEER + SUCKER makes BEERSUCKER; swapping its leading B for S gives the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a puckered cotton fabric, often striped, used for summer clothes.

clue.text: What might be sung in shed

definitions.meaning: a sea song sailors sing while working

explanation.surface: A song that might be performed inside a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a sailors' work song and a rough cabin or hut.

clue.text: Make effort to restrain piano virtuoso

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the musical letter is held inside the verb for striving

parts.note: to exert oneself is to make an effort
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Advice to a virtuoso pianist to work hard at holding back.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a highly skilled performer, a master or specialist in their field.

clue.text: Kit that's sillier yet working without batteries

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scrambled letters sit around the word for kit
the letters of sillier yet are worked into a new order

parts.note: kit, as in equipment, is gear

explanation.surface: Some kit looks even sillier when it works without batteries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: the anagram SIETILLERY wraps round GEAR, giving SIE-GEAR-TILLERY. 'Batteries' suggests power cells, but means groups of big guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery batteries are units of heavy guns, and siege artillery is the heavy ordnance used to bombard fortifications.

clue.text: Clegg's friend certain to show calmness

parts.note: Compo was Clegg's friend in the long-running BBC sitcom Last of the Summer Wine
certain means sure

explanation.surface: Clegg's mate, confident enough to show a cool head.
explanation.walkthrough: Clegg suggests the politician Nick Clegg, but here he is a character from Last of the Summer Wine, a British TV comedy about pensioners in Yorkshire, whose friend was Compo.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a settled, unruffled state of mind; they are near synonyms.

clue.text: Olympic medallist taking time off from sport

indicators.note: taking one thing off from another means removing it, so the letter for time is dropped from the game

parts.note: tennis is a sport

explanation.surface: An Olympian taking a break from their sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Jessica Ennis(-Hill) is a British heptathlete who won Olympic gold in London in 2012.
explanation.definitionFit: Jessica Ennis is a named example of an athlete who won an Olympic medal.

clue.text: Prevent onset of bee sting

parts.note: to bar is to prevent

indicators.note: the onset of something is its start, so the first letter of bee is taken

explanation.surface: Advice on stopping a bee before it stings.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is the sharp point of a hook or sting, and also a stinging remark.

clue.text: Miss flying air taxi that's set out about five

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about, that is around, the Roman numeral
the letters of air taxi are set out afresh in a new order

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A young woman travelling by air taxi, with five passengers aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's set out' makes AIATRIX from air taxi, and V goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviatrix is an old-fashioned term for a female pilot, a woman who flies.

clue.text: Sticking weapons in horse set on running

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse

indicators.note: running suggests the letters of set on are in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Weapons poked into a horse that has been set running.
explanation.definitionFit: Bayonets are blades fixed to rifles for stabbing, so weapons used for sticking.

clue.text: They're often blocks landlords with money to invest put up front

indicators.note: in this down clue the money goes at the top, in front of the landlords

parts.note: capital is money available to invest
landlords let property, so they are letters

explanation.surface: Landlords who use investment funds to pay deposits up front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocks' looks like blocks of flats, fitting the landlords, but refers to block capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing in block capitals means using upper-case characters, so these are often blocks.

clue.text: Brand of computer program mostly needed for this product

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: an applet is a small computer program

explanation.surface: A program needed for a particular make of computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple is the company behind the Mac computers, a well-known computing brand.

clue.text: Improve a financial centre's dishonesty

parts.note: to mend is to fix or improve
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: Cleaning up the lying in a financial centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The City (of London) is the UK's banking district.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendacity is the habit of lying, untruthfulness.

clue.text: Wreck right to enter depot going round and round?

indicators.note: the letter for right goes into the reversed word
going round means turning back, so depot is read backwards

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A vehicle going round and round inside a depot ends up wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' reverses DEPOT to TOPED; R enters it for TORPED, and O follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo a plan is to wreck or sink it, figuratively blowing it up.

clue.text: Overall, Henman's head over heels in love

indicators.note: turned head over heels, the letters are flipped end to end

parts.note: net means overall, as in a net result
Tim Henman is a British tennis player, so Henman's becomes Tim's

explanation.surface: A tennis star tumbling for someone completely.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Henman was Britain's leading men's tennis player around 2000. 'head over heels' also suggests being in love, but here it reverses NETTIMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being smitten means being infatuated, struck by romantic feeling.

clue.text: One engaged by president is put in to stop gloating over victory

indicators.note: the numeral is held, as if engaged, inside the president's name

parts.note: Donald Trump is a US president
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the word for stop

parts.note: to halt is to stop

explanation.surface: A president hiring someone and stepping in to stop the gloating.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone triumphalist exults excessively in a win.

clue.text: Scent what Presbyterians oppose vocally

indicators.note: vocally signals a word said aloud to give a near-identical sound

parts.note: popery is a hostile term for Roman Catholicism, which Presbyterians historically opposed

explanation.surface: A smell that Presbyterians speak out against.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a bowl of dried petals and spices kept for its fragrance.

clue.text: We locals prepared salad

indicators.note: prepared as a dish is, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Local people making a salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a salad of shredded cabbage in mayonnaise.

clue.text: Lovely fit girl comes in

indicators.note: the girl's name comes into the middle of the other word

parts.note: able means fit, as in able-bodied
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A pretty, athletic girl walks through the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means charming and delightful, roughly synonymous with lovely.

clue.text: Incredible story Wilde's valet fabricated after love

indicators.note: the anagram comes after the letter for love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

indicators.note: fabricated means made up, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde's manservant inventing a tall tale about romance.
explanation.definitionFit: An old wives' tale is a widely held superstition or myth, not to be believed.

clue.text: Stop back

definitions.meaning: rear, as in the hind legs

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to impede; as an adjective it means at the rear.

clue.text: Attack daily grind enthusiastically at first

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British cleaning woman who comes in daily

indicators.note: at first means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Attacking the daily routine with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, or daily, is an old British term for a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a headlong rush at an enemy, a form of attack.

clue.text: What might keep a listener warm?

definitions.text: What might keep a listener warm?

parts.words: What might keep a listener warm?
parts.note: a listener is something that listens, here an ear, and a flap on a hat covers it

explanation.definitionFit: An earflap is the part of a cap that folds down to cover the ears against cold.

clue.text: One old prime minister or another gets a kind of bread

parts.words: One old prime minister or another
parts.note: William Pitt the Elder and his son Pitt the Younger were both British prime ministers

explanation.surface: A former PM getting some bread.
explanation.walkthrough: The a is used twice? No: 'a' is taken as written, and 'kind of bread' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, hollow bread from the Middle East.

clue.text: East German with lots of money, one sticking their head in the sand?

definitions.text: one sticking their head in the sand?

parts.note: Ost is German for east
having lots of money is being rich

explanation.surface: A wealthy East German who ignores reality.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is famed, wrongly, for burying its head in the sand to avoid danger.

clue.text: I'll deliver crude oil with barter

indicators.note: crude suggests the letters are in a rough, unrefined state and need rearranging

explanation.surface: An oil trader promising delivery of crude in exchange for goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude oil' reads as a phrase, but 'crude' is the anagram signal for oil and barter.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberator sets people free, delivering them from oppression.

clue.text: Tree having been around longer

definitions.meaning: a small tree with white flowers and dark berries

explanation.surface: A tree that has stood longer than others.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a shrub or tree; elder also means older of two people.

clue.text: Small, ultimately stunted and unwanted plant

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of stunted

explanation.surface: A small, stunted plant nobody wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed is any plant growing where it is not wanted.

clue.text: Food served here is appetiser, fresh, penny off

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A restaurant offering a fresh appetiser at a penny discount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' says the P is removed from IS APPETISER before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A patisserie is a pastry shop where cakes are sold and eaten.
